meta.title: Competitor Radar
meta.niche: AI talent agents and job-search tools that help startup job seekers get hired (matching, introductions to hiring managers, auto-apply)

analysis.summary: Wonsulting and JobCopilot publish fast, mostly job-seeker advice. Jack & Jill targets hiring teams. Clera, Wellfound and Jobright AI published nothing new in 30 days.

points.text: Wonsulting leads on volume: 22 new pages and 12 updated ones, mostly newsletter advice plus a refresh of its product pages.
Jack & Jill's six new pages mostly speak to employers: hiring guides, a startup hiring report and an Attio case study.
JobCopilot posted 11 new pages, 10 of them how-to guides on resumes, networking and safe auto-apply, plus one white-label partner page.

Clera.play: 12 pages and no new or updated pages in the last 30 days.

Jack & Jill.play: Hiring guides, a startup hiring report and customer stories to win employers. Also 302 company pages.

Wellfound.play: 85 pages, no new or updated pages this period. No clear play to read.

Jobright AI.play: 61 pages, no new or updated pages this period. No clear play to read.

JobCopilot.play: Many job-search how-tos, a safe auto-apply guide, one rival review, and a white-label offer.

WonsultingAI.play: Weekly-style newsletter advice, refreshed product and coaching pages, plus a 144-page job-search hub.
WonsultingAI.aimed: Job seekers, from students to experienced

shared.title: Networking and outreach advice
shared.text: Both teach job seekers to message recruiters and get referrals: JobCopilot on cold emails and informational interviews, Wonsulting on LinkedIn messages and follow-ups. Clera can show its introductions solve this.

shared.title: Resume and ATS guides
shared.text: Both publish how-tos on ATS (software that screens resumes) and resume writing. It is crowded, general advice, so it is hard to stand out with.

shared.title: Pages built at scale
shared.text: Jack & Jill has 302 company pages and Wonsulting has 144 job-search hub pages. Both use templates to cover many searches.

gaps.title: Startup-specific job seeker guides
gaps.text: Competitor how-tos are general: resumes, gaps, salary. Nobody writes about startup roles, equity, or how to judge an early-stage company.

gaps.title: How AI introductions work, and why to trust them
gaps.text: JobCopilot covers safe auto-apply. Nobody explains matching and warm intros to hiring managers in plain English.

gaps.title: Candidate stories from startup hires
gaps.text: Wonsulting tells job seeker stories; Jack & Jill's case is from the employer side. Few stories show a startup candidate's full journey.

versus.Jack & Jill: Far bigger site, six new pages in 30 days, mostly aimed at employers; Clera has 12 pages and no new ones.
versus.Wellfound: Larger site at 85 pages, but no new or updated pages this period, so it is no faster than Clera.
versus.Jobright AI: 61 pages and no recent activity, so like Clera it is quiet; its larger library is the only edge.
versus.JobCopilot: Publishes about 11 pages a month on general job-search help, while Clera published none and is narrower on startups.
versus.WonsultingAI: Much larger and more active, with 22 new and 12 updated pages; Clera has 12 pages and no activity.
